Question: What is the review of the Adipurush movie?
Answer: Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Ram, is an anime co-produced by India and Japan in the year 1993. All the characters from the actual epic have been so well depicted in this movie: Right from Lord Ram’s calm to Ravana’s vengeance. Lakshman’s brotherhood to Hanuman’s respect for Lord Ram and Sita. There was zero vulgarity in dialogues. Heck you could sense some level of respect when Lord Ram and Ravana addressed each other. Dialogues containing respectful addresses like “Site” “Pitaji” “Pitashri” “Aap” was a treat to our ears. Now, let’s address the elephant in the room (sorry to insult the elephant). Adipurush seems like a movie where the director and the cast met in a club, drank a lot and the director said “Hey, let’s make a Kalyug, chapri version of one the greatest Hindu epic- Ramayana” and all are like “Hell yeah. And to top that, let’s do it with zero research”. “What went wrong in the movie?”, you might ask. FYI The writer of Adipurush, Manoj Muntashir, said in pre-release interviews, “Not even 1% of the movie has been deviated from the original Ramayana”. Kya fhook ke aaya hai bey? 🤨 Adipurush is a total disaster and I hope it stays that way in box office as well. I feel makers of such movies are not at much fault as much as the audiences. No matter what the story is, Indian audiences watch movies based on cast and masala content. And it’s proven over time with movies casting Bhai, SRK being a super hit even though the story is crap. Why do you think Bollywood has more action and masala movies than sci-fi/mystery/thriller movies? You get what you want. Only way to discourage movie makers from creating such movies is to not watch it and let it flop in the box-office. That’s my take on Adipurush. Peace. Image courtesy: Google. Edit 1: I realised minutes ago about this trivial fact. The english voice over of Lord Ram in 1993 anime Ramayana was done by Bryan Cranston (lead star of Breaking Bad).

Question: As a software engineer, what frustrates you about the hiring process?
Answer: Scene 1: Consultant: We are looking for a candidate with minimum 4+ years of experience with good exposure on Java, Node.js, Python, Kafka, SQL, NoSQL, React.js, HTML, AWS/GCP is a plus. Me: I have worked on all these technologies. Consultant: That’s great. What’s your current CTC? Me: XYZ Consultant: And how much are you expecting? Me: ABC Consultant: Oh! That’s around… (takes 5sec to calculate) Me: I know, 45% hike. Consultant: Why so much hike? Me: As per your JD, you need a full-stack dev, and I fit those requirements. Getting there wasn’t easy for me, it took me efforts, thousands of hours of online courses, spent weekends with my laptop, …… Consultant: That’s good, but we can offer just 20%. Me: Have a nice day then! They expect tons, but offer peanuts! Scene 2: (Before the interview) HR: How much are you expecting? Me: 45% hike. HR: Cool. Let me setup your interview. (Post selection) HR: We can offer you 30%. Me: But we had already agreed upon 45% before the interview. Plus my interview went quite well. HR: No doubt there’s good feedback from panels, but as per the companies budget, 30% is what we can offer. Me: Thanks for wasting my time. We are lured by fake promises. Scene 3: HR: Hey. The panels really liked the assignment you submitted. For further rounds, we require you to come down to our office which is in Bangalore. Me: Shouldn’t we have a telephonic or skype before onsite? HR: No. This is the process. Don’t worry about expenses, we will reimburse it. I got rejected in the 1st onsite f2f interview. Got the feedback as “The first design problem you solved was good, but the 2nd one, that one could have been done using some_tech_which_I_never_worked_on. But instead you used the_one_I_had_expertise_on.” Me: Was that some_tech_which_I_never_worked_on mentioned on my resume? Panel: Nope. Me: Then how can you expect me to know something which I have 0 expertise on? Panel: Because that’s what we use here. Me: Then you should have rejected me during resume screening itself, or at least had a telephonic round. Travelling to Bangalore isn’t a joke. HR: Makes sense. But you should have gone through our career site. The stack is mentioned there. Me: I went through the JD sent to me. No stack was mentioned there. Plus none of the panels were aware that I had travelled all the way from Mumbai for this interview. Anyways, I have a flight to catch. Thanks for the opportunity. Some HR’s will do anything to meet their targets. Scene 4 and the most common, frustrating scenario of all: HR: Hey! Congrats. You are selected. Me: Great, thanks. HR: Before I release the offer, kindly send me your last 3 months salary slips. Once sent: HR: Oh, we will also require your joining CTC in current organisation and also your latest appraisal letter with salary breakup. Me: How is that relevant? HR: It’s part of the process, we need it. Once sent: HR: So your appraisal took place just a couple of months back and you are asking for 45%? Me: I don’t see how that matters, but yes. HR: We can’t offer you that much. Me: I am used to this now. Thanks for the opportunity.

Question: What is your favorite movie scene that gives you goosebumps every time you watch it?
Answer: There are 2 scenes from the movie The Schindler’s List which gives me chills every time I watch it. There’s a crucial scene between Goeth and Schindler where they both sit atop Goeth’s villa in the concentration camp. Goeth is too drunk, as Schindler slowly sips his drink. They both discuss the definition of power. Goeth: You are never drunk. You know that’s… that’s a little control. Control is power. That’s… power. Schindler: Is that why they fear us? Goeth: We have the fucking power to kill, that's why they fear us. Schindler: They fear us because we have the power to kill arbitrarily. A man commits a crime, he should know better. We have him killed, and we feel pretty good about it. Or we kill him ourselves and we feel even better. That's not power though. That's justice. It's different than power. Power is when we have every justification to kill, and we don't. Goeth: You think that's power? Schindler: That's what the emperors had. A man stole something, he's brought in before the emperor, he throws himself down on the ground, he begs for mercy. He knows he's going to die. And the emperor pardons him. This worthless man, he lets him go. Goeth believes that fear drives power. The way Schindler tries manipulating Goeth by attacking the problem at it’s core is remarkable. The second scene is where Schindler leaves his factory for good as the war is over and he is sure to be hunted as a member of the Nazi party. Schindler: I could have got more out. I could have got more. I don't know. If I'd just... I could have got more. Stern: Oskar, there are eleven hundred people who are alive because of you. Look at them. Schindler: If I'd made more money... I threw away so much money. You have no idea. If I'd just... Stern: There will be generations because of what you did. Schindler: I didn't do enough! Stern: You did so much. Schindler: This car. Goeth would have bought this car. Why did I keep the car? Ten people right there. Ten people. Ten more people. Schindler: This pin. Two people. This is gold. Two more people. He would have given me two for it, at least one. One more person. A person, Stern. For this. Schindler: I could have gotten one more person... and I didn't! And I... I didn't! This scene literally moved me. Image source: YouTube.

Question: What is your biggest mistake or regret?
Answer: Buying this notebook from U.S via a friend. A $1100 HP Spectre X360 Notebook. $1100 which I withdrew from my provident fund account. I was so excited the day my friend landed. Little did I know that the excitement will be short lived. Our strategies didn’t go as planned and the laptop got caught in customs (my friend was carrying his own laptop too, unknowingly). Had to pay INR 32,000 as custom duty. So basically, the total price I had to pay for this notebook was same as what it costed in India. Disaster! The next day was my joining day in a startup. They gave me a brand new Macbook Pro. Major facepalm! Now I forced myself to use my notebook on weekends to justify the cost I paid for it. One fine night after binge watching a TV series, I kept my notebook on my desk on charging mode, next to my water bottle. Next day I woke up only to realise that the bottle was lying on the floor, empty. The notebook was drenched with a chemical compound consisting of 2 atoms of Hydrogen and 1 atom of oxygen, otherwise called water. I disconnected the notebook immediately, wiped it clean and kept it in a rice bag for 3 days. Called a technician who, after inspection, inferred “It’s too late. The motherboard is fried”. These words were more deadlier than “I think we should break up”. The price for a new motherboard was INR 26,000. Buying this expensive notebook was my worst investment which I regret till date. The laptop, still fried, is kept in my never-to-open shelf. Edit 1: Some people are telling me to stop crying and saying that this is a small mistake:

Question: What is the difference between a programmer and a developer?
Answer: A programmer is someone who would spend most or all of his time in front of his system coding. They are responsible for writing, testing, debugging/troubleshooting and maintaining the source code of computer programs. A programmer is like a cook in a restaurant. On the other hand, a software developer is more like a professional chef. Not only can they cook to a high standard, but they can take a more creative and conceptual approach to what they’re making. This means finding out what their target market wants, creating a plan for how to make it, and coming up with a series of instructions that they can give to other cooks. Chefs do this for restaurants and software developers do this for programmers. Programmers are all about code. It is their job to take the specifications given to them by a developer and turn them into a functioning application. To do this they put the developer’s ideas into a language that the computer can understand and follow. Software developers can be thought of as project managers who can code while programmers are technicians. When comparing a programmer and a developer, a developer should be able to code but their main job is finding ways to solve problems. To do this, they need to figure out what those problems are and then figure out the technical framework for solving them.

Question: Why aren't bullets sharp?
Answer: Because they don't need to be. At the speed with which bullets are fired, which is about 350 m/s for an average bullet, even a round tip bullet can easily penetrate human skin. The goal is to maximize the accuracy, reduce resistance when it's in air and increase the damage caused to the target. These are hollow-point bullets, one of the deadliest one's. They have a small pit at the apex. When this bullet hits a soft target, the pressure in the hollow tip causes the bullet to expand outwards. This is called mushrooming as the resultant bullet looks like one. The greater frontal surface area of the expanded bullet limits its depth of penetration into the target, and causes more extensive tissue damage along the wound path. Military bullets are often pointy, but that's mostly because of aerodynamics (streamline bullets cause less drag than rounded one's). While these bullets are the most aerodynamic, they are also the worst in terms of length, because they have the highest ogive[1] to cylinder ratio. This is not usually a problem for rifles (which is why you will find a lot of pointy ended spitzer type rifle bullets), but it's a bad situation for a handgun, where the length of the bullet massively increases the size of the magazine and chamber for a pistol. It's even worse for revolvers, because they have a huge and heavy metal cylinder (not the same as the bullet cylinder) which holds all rounds. Question: What is the most interesting fact that you know and I don't, but I should?
Answer: Do you remember this popular nursery rhyme? Ringa ringa roses, Pocket full of posies Husha busha! We all fall down! Yes. This is the Indian version. Let's check out other versions too. British Ring-a-ring o' roses, A pocket full of posies, A-tishoo! A-tishoo! We all fall down. American Ring-a-round the roses, A pocket full of posies, Ashes! Ashes! We all fall down. German Ringel ringel reihen, Wir sind der Kinder dreien, sitzen unter'm Hollerbusch Und machen alle Husch husch husch! Sounds cute? Let's check the origin and it's meaning as per wiki. In 1898, A Dictionary of British Folklore contained the belief that an explanation of the game was of pagan origin, based on the Sheffield Glossary comparison of Jacob Grimm's Deutsche Mythologie. The theory states that it is in reference to Pagan myths and cited a passage which states, "Gifted children of fortune have the power to laugh roses, as Freyja wept gold." Believing the first instance to be indicative of Pagan beings of light. Another suggestion is more literal, that it was making a "ring" around the roses and bowing with the all "fall down" as a curtsy. In 1892, the American writer, Eugene Field wrote a poem titled Teeny-Weenythat specifically referred to fey folk playing ring-a-rosie. According to Games and Songs of American Children, published in 1883, the "rosie" was a reference to the French word for rose tree and the children would dance and stoop to the person in the center. Variations, especially more literal ones, were identified and noted with the literal falling down that would sever the connections to the game-rhyme. Again in 1898, sneezing was then noted to be indicative of many superstitious and supernatural beliefs across differing cultures. Since the 20th century, the rhyme has often been associated with the Great Plague which happened in England in 1665, or with earlier outbreaks of the Black Death in England. Interpreters of the rhyme before the Second World War make no mention of this; by 1951, however, it seems to have become well established as an explanation for the form of the rhyme that had become standard in the United Kingdom. Peter and Iona Opie, the leading authorities on nursery rhymes, remarked: The invariable sneezing and falling down in modern English versions have given would-be origin finders the opportunity to say that the rhyme dates back to the Great Plague. A rosy rash, they allege, was a symptom of the plague, and posies of herbs were carried as protection and to ward off the smell of the disease. Sneezing or coughing was a final fatal symptom, and "all fall down" was exactly what happened. The line Ashes, Ashes in colonial versions of the rhyme is claimed to refer variously to cremation of the bodies, the burning of victims' houses, or blackening of their skin, and the theory has been adapted to be applied to other versions of the rhyme. In its various forms, the interpretation has entered into popular culture and has been used elsewhere to make oblique reference to the plague. Folklore scholars regard the theory as baseless for several reasons: So much for a simple nursery rhyme! :-)

Question: What is your review of the Avengers 4: Endgame teaser trailer (December 2018)?
Answer: The traile… oops! The teaser gave a glimpse (a really short one) of the movie, but with hidden messages, which most comic fanatics might have noticed. Endgame references from Avengers: Infinity war And Avengers: Age of Ultron This brief moment in Age of Ultron isn’t just important to Endgame simply because it drops the title. It’s important because the moment as a whole is there to remind the Avengers why they’re there. Not just to protect the people of Earth from themselves, but to protect them from even greater threats, that Tony has seen up-close and personal, that could destroy their entire world. Tony lost in space This much-anticipated trailer starts with a shot of Iron Man's helmet, badly broken in the wake of his last fight with Thanos. He's seemingly all alone on a spaceship, without power, floating along. He's recording a message to Pepper Potts on his helmet, adding in a little humor. This could be immediately following the end of Infinity War, which would imply that Nebula (Karen Gillan) is potentially on the same ship. This is Nebula’s hand which, I assume, is touching Tony's shoulder. Thanos scarecrow Thanos is briefly shown tilling the fields on his quiet farm, basking in the glory of having just murdered half of all life in the universe. And as he does so, the trailer features a shot of his old armor, now propped up as a bizarre sort of scarecrow. This scene draws inspiration directly from the 1991's comics Infinity Gauntlet Thanos is actually shown retiring from villainy and tilling the fields on a remote alien world. In that story, Thanos is retreating in disgrace more than gloating over a hard-won victory. As in the movie, Thanos acquires the full Infinity Gauntlet in this story and uses it to wipe out half of all life in the universe. The difference is that he quickly loses the Gauntlet due to his own hubris and has his work quickly undone. Thanos realizes that deep down, he always wanted to lose. Faced with his own psychological weakness, Thanos retires to live a quiet, simple life. He even uses his costume as a scarecrow just as he does in this movie. Ronin Jeremy Renner suited up in black and gold, weilding a weird katana-esque blade on the streets of a rainy Japanese city. Ronin was an identity that Clint Barton used, instead of Hawkeye, from about 2007 to 2010 in Marvel Comics. Why the name, costume and weapons change? Well, in 2004, Clint died. Then, in 2007, he was brought back to life. While he was dead, the world had necessarily moved on. A young avenger named Kate Bishop was calling herself Hawkeye — and wearing a purple costume and using trick arrows — and Clint thought she was doing pretty well with the name. Wishing additionally to hide his return from the wider world for a bit, he borrowed a code name, costume and weapons from a fallen Avenger, Maya Lopez, to become Ronin. In Avengers: Endgame, he may have darker motivations. For all we knew, in Infinity War, Clint Barton had retired from the superhero game. A tie in comic and the movie itself confirmed that he’d taken a plea deal after breaking the Sokovia Accords in Captain America: Civil War, and returned home to his family's farm. What could have dragged him away from his wife and kids? “We lost, all of us,” Captain America says in the Endgame trailer. But he says “we lost family” just as the trailer cuts to Clint in Japan, moodily wiping his blade on one arm. Did Clint Barton’s family survive the snap? Odds are not looking so good. Scott Lang Avengers: Endgame’s trailer sets up a surprising reveal: the surviving Avengers presumed that Scott Lang, aka Ant-Man, was killed when Thanos wiped out half of the universe’s life, only to have him turn up on their doorstep at the end of the trailer. A post-credits scene from Ant-Man and the Wasp explains that while other people on Earth were shattering into dust following Thanos’ snap, Ant-Man was in the quantum realm. Ant-Man may not have been killed by Thanos’ snap — officially referred to as the Decimation, according to Marvel Comics — possibly because he wasn’t within the universe at the time. While Lang is exploring the quantum realm, he’s warned to look out for time vortexes, whose name implies that if he passes through, could reconfigure time itself. This means when Lang teams up with the Avengers — or the remaining Avengers — they could use those time vortexes to reverse time and save the population from devastation. How Scott gets out of the quantum realm is a mystery. Now, the issue with Avengers trailers — or any movie trailer — is you can’t trust them. Remember that the Hulk starred in Avengers: Infinity War’s trailers and then never appeared in the actual film. This could just be a cool gesture to throw fans from guessing what’s going to happen — like we are — but this does help to explain how the Avengers could possibly defeat Thanos going forward. Did I love the trailer? Absolutely!!! Question: What made you quit your job?
Answer: After 2 years and 2 months of working in a product based organization (Zycus Infotech, Mumbai) as a Software developer and learning lots of new tech, I left the company as work had become monotous. Joined an MNC (Oracle Financial Services and Software), with a decent hike and hopes of working on new tech. First month @OFSS: My local desktop was setup with few softwares in the first week. Client side desktop, which we connect to via VPN was partially setup at the end of first month. Basically, I had no work for this month, no softwares to learn new things (installing development related softwares in local machine was prohibited). Used online compilers for the same. Even that was blocked after few days :(. Imagine, Stack Overflow - Where Developers Learn, Share, & Build Careers was blocked in my ODC. Second month @OFSS: Remote desktop was fully setup with roles and permissions to servers and tools and work was allocated with no bar on deadline. Realized I was allocated to the project as a Support engineer (was totally disappointed). I was in my comfort zone, doing work with speed of a snail. Came in late and left early as manager was onsite and there was no one senior to track the ins and the outs. Eventually, had to join companies free services (gym, indoor games and sleeping area) to kill time. Third month @OFSS: Work had become monotonous which mostly involved solving existing bugs and other support level activities. Continued my extracurricular activities like going to gym, playing TT and carom, cricket and badminton, sleeping in sleeping area for an hour, etc. Fourth month @OFSS: By now, my weekdays went as follows: Oh, and did I mention I also went to watch movies between 12pm to 3pm? :P Fifth month @OFSS: Well, I had become good at playing carom and TT, and looked fit by now. But wait! Had I learnt anything related to my profession in these past 4 months? Did I develop something incredible that I can put in my resume? NO! Actually, I was forgetting the techs I learnt in my 2 years of exp. This is the moment I realized I have to stop being in my comfort zone. Tried analyzing which project I could switch to to enhance my skills, but found nothing. Most projects were using outdated techs, rest had no vacancy. Decided to learn by self and build my resume. Sixth month @OFSS: Still worked with the speed of snail, but learnt new techs at the speed light (well obviously not with the speed of light :p) and built my own projects in my spare time. Built a strong resume and posted it on job portals. Started giving interviews. Rejected many due to less hike (no one was meeting my expectations as I was leaving my current organization within 6 months). Also was rejected by a few. Learnt from rejections and gave more interviews! Currently, I am working with a product based startup. Services they offer are not much compared to MNC's but the work is awesome with lots of new techs, which requires continuous learning. Salary they offered was what I had asked for. FYI, now I just spend 30 min tops on extra-curriculars as deadlines have bars now. :) Life begins at the end of your comfort zone - Neale Donald Walsch

Question: What is the difference between reference variable and object in Java?
Answer: Reference variables and Objects are completely different concepts, however, they are related to each other. Reference variables holds reference to an object in heap. Basically it's an address to where the object is stored. In the above example, variable emp holds a reference to an object of class Employee residing in heap. This reference variable can later be used to manipulate the state of an object. Objects reside in Heap memory. Local reference variables reside in a method frame inside a thread stack whereas instance and class variables reside in heap as they are part of object. Food for thought: Objects are garbage collected when there is no reference variable pointing to it. However, there is no guarantee of this though (depends on GC algorithm implemented by the JVM). Question: How is x^0 is 1 and not 0 ? Can anyone explain?
Answer: This is a very good question. Let's start with the basics first. x^n means we are multiplying x with itself n times. When we raise a number to the zeroth power, that means we multiply the number by itself zero times - but that means we're not multiplying anything at all! When we add 0 to a number, we get the same number (duhh…right?). Here, 0 is an additive identity (the only number which when added to another number, doesn't change the value of that number, x+0=x). So, by this reasoning, it makes sense that if adding no numbers at all gives back the additive identity, multiplying no numbers at all should give the multiplicative identity. Now, what's the multiplicative identity? Well, it's the only number which can be multiplied by any other number without changing that other number. In short, the multiplicative identity is the number 1, because for any other number x, 1*x = x. So, the reason that any number to the zero power is one is because any number to the zero power is just the product of no numbers at all, which is the multiplicative identity, 1.
